description: Shows what one material does to a glaze, by putting more and more of it into a base recipe (an ingredient blend or progression test: whiting 0 to 20, say, in 2 to 11 tiles). With mode "add" (the default) it goes on top of the base, so the recipe grows; with mode "replace" the same amount comes out of another material of the base (`instead`), so the total stays the same. Each tile has its amount of the material, its recipe in percent, its key unity formula figures (silica, alumina, boron, the fluxes), silica to alumina, calculated expansion, its place on Stull's chart (stull: region, crazed), the names of the limit cautions it has, and, with a firing, whether its chemistry fits that firing (coneFit verdict). trend sums up what moves from the first tile to the last, and which Stull regions the tiles cross. Give base materials only, no colorants. This is a calculation from published figures, not a test result: the tiles, fired, decide, and the cautions are guides, not a guarantee of food safety.

firing.description: The firing, as a cone or a temperature. Leave it out when it is not known. From cone 12 up (about 1320 °C) no published glaze limits reach, so the limits are not checked there; the cone check judges cone 06 to 10 only.

chart.description: Which cones the cone is: Orton (the default) or SK (JIS R 8101).

cone.description: An Orton cone from 022 to 42 ("06", "6", "10", "14", a half cone as "5.5"), or with chart "sk" an SK cone (JIS R 8101) from SK 022 to SK 20 ("6a", "8", "14").

from.description: The least of it, in the unit the recipe lines share (default 0: the base alone).

instead.description: With mode "replace": the material of the base that gives way to it.

language.description: The language for any sentences in the answer, as a BCP 47 tag such as "en", "de" or "ja". Languages Glazecalc does not offer are answered in English.

limitSet.description: The limits to check against, as check_limits takes it: "glazecalc" (the default) or "hesselberth-roy".

material.description: The material to vary, by its library name (search_materials finds it), such as "Whiting".

mode.description: "add" (the default): put the material on top of the base. "replace": take the same amount out of `instead`, so the total stays the same.

recipe.description: The base recipe the material goes into.

amount.description: Its amount in the recipe, in any unit the other lines share (grams, parts, percent).

analysis.description: Only for a material not in the library: its oxides in weight percent, as { "SiO2": 68.5, "Al2O3": 17.4 }.

loi.description: Its loss on ignition in percent, with an analysis.

material.description: The material, by its name in the Glazecalc library ("Custer Spar", "Whiting", "EPK"), or your own name when you give its analysis.

steps.description: Tiles from from to to (2 to 11, default 5).

to.description: The most of it, in the unit the recipe lines share: it must be more than from.

name: vary_material
title: What one material does across a range
